hints: Because the block is on the point of sliding up the plane, the friction force $F$ acts down the plane opposing motion.
Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane: $65\cos 36^\circ - 12g\sin 24^\circ - F = 0$, and calculate $F$.
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane: $R + 65\sin 36^\circ - 12g\cos 24^\circ = 0$, find $R$, and use $\mu = \frac{F}{R}$.
walkthrough:
Identify all forces acting on the $12\text{ kg}$ block:
- Weight: $W = mg = (12)(10) = 120\text{ N}$ vertically downwards
- Normal reaction: $R$ perpendicular to and directed out of the plane
- Tension in the string: $65\text{ N}$ at an angle of $36^\circ$ above the line of greatest slope
- Friction force: $F$ acting down the plane, because the block is on the verge of sliding up the plane

Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane:
Taking the uphill direction as positive:
$$\sum F_{\parallel} = 0$$
$$65\cos 36^\circ - mg\sin 24^\circ - F = 0$$
Substitute $mg = 120\text{ N}$:
$$65\cos 36^\circ - 120\sin 24^\circ - F = 0$$
Evaluate the trigonometric terms:
$$65\cos 36^\circ \approx 65(0.809017) = 52.5861\text{ N}$$
$$120\sin 24^\circ \approx 120(0.406737) = 48.8084\text{ N}$$
$$52.5861 - 48.8084 - F = 0$$
$$F = 52.5861 - 48.8084 = 3.7777\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane:
Taking the upward normal direction as positive:
$$\sum F_{\perp} = 0$$
$$R + 65\sin 36^\circ - mg\cos 24^\circ = 0$$
$$R = 120\cos 24^\circ - 65\sin 36^\circ$$
Evaluate the trigonometric terms:
$$120\cos 24^\circ \approx 120(0.913545) = 109.6254\text{ N}$$
$$65\sin 36^\circ \approx 65(0.587785) = 38.2060\text{ N}$$
$$R = 109.6254 - 38.2060 = 71.4194\text{ N}$$

Apply the limiting friction condition $F = \mu R$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{3.7777}{71.4194} \approx 0.052895$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $\mu = 0.0529$.
